exposure: additional maternal cardiac risk factors (congestive heart failure, arrhythmia, pulmonary circulation disorders, chronic hypertension)
cohort: The study included an estimated 40,780,439 delivery hospitalizations between 2010 and 2020, with 35,242 involving mothers with a congenital heart disease diagnosis.
finding: Deliveries with maternal congenital heart disease were associated with increased odds of 60-day postpartum readmission and more severe complications during readmissions compared to those without.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery (both primary and repeat) was significantly associated with increased odds of 60-day postpartum readmission among women with congenital heart disease.
